title: Aggregate Products into an Array Per Category
description:
For each product category aggregate all product names into an array and count how many products are in each category.

**Table: products** — `id`, `name`, `category`

Output columns: `category`, `product_names`, `product_count`. Order by `category`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE products (id INT, name VARCHAR, category VARCHAR); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Widget A','Electronics'),(2,'Widget B','Electronics'),(3,'Gadget X','Electronics'),(4,'Shirt Pro','Clothing'),(5,'Shirt Lite','Clothing'),(6,'Pants X','Clothing'),(7,'Book Alpha','Books'),(8,'Book Beta','Books');
solution_sql: SELECT category, ARRAY_AGG(name ORDER BY name) AS product_names, COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM products GROUP BY category ORDER BY category

test_cases.description: 3 categories: Books (2 products), Clothing (3 products), Electronics (3 products)

hints: ARRAY_AGG(name ORDER BY name) collects all name values within the group into an ordered array.
In DuckDB you can also use LIST(name ORDER BY name) — both return an array/list type column.
explanation: ARRAY_AGG is an aggregate function that collects values into an array rather than a scalar. GROUP BY category produces one row per category. Books: ['Book Alpha', 'Book Beta'] (count=2). Clothing: ['Pants X', 'Shirt Lite', 'Shirt Pro'] (count=3). Electronics: ['Gadget X', 'Widget A', 'Widget B'] (count=3). Arrays are useful for passing structured data to application layers.
